name: Signed Ideal of a Downset Filter
statement: If $C$ is downward closed in a coordinate block $U$, $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^U$ is a nonempty downset with minimal nonfaces $\mathcal N(D)$, and $F=\{x\in C:x|_U\in D\}$, then $Q_F=Q_C+(\prod_{j\in J}x_{j,1}:J\in\mathcal N(D))$.
proof: A consistent partial pattern missing from $F$ either was already missing from $C$, or has a witness in $C$. Lower every unspecified coordinate of $U$ in that witness to zero. Downward closure retains membership in $C$ and the prescribed pattern. Since the resulting word is not in $F$, its prescribed one-set in $U$ contains a minimal nonface of $D$. This proves both generator containments; minimal consistent generators suffice for the monomial-ideal equality.
comments: This identity retains literal signs and is stronger than the corresponding unsigned shattered-support formula.
